mechanism_narrative: An increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals labor market weakness, which may lead to negative S&P 500 returns as investor sentiment deteriorates.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive returns in 60% of cases when UNRATE increases, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) exceeds 4.5%, it indicates monetary tightening, leading to negative S&P 500 returns as borrowing costs rise.
failure_condition: If positive returns occur in over 50% of cases when FEDFUNDS >4.5%, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous growth in real estate starts (HOUST) and consumer spending (RSAFS) indicates strong demand, leading to positive S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: If returns are negative in 40% of cases with positive HOUST and RSAFS growth, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Industrial production (INDPRO) growth during late-cycle expansion signals supply strength, leading to positive S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: If returns are negative in 35% of cases with INDPRO growth, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: GDP growth (GDPC1) indicates strong economic activity, leading to positive S&P 500 returns as corporate earnings improve.
failure_condition: If GDPC1 growth doesn't correlate with positive returns (p > 0.05), the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A significant increase in payroll employment (PAYEMS) signals a strong labor market, leading to positive S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: If returns are negative in 40% of cases with PAYEMS increase, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: Rising FEDFUNDS alongside falling UNRATE indicates a strong economy with tightening monetary policy, leading to negative S&P 500 returns.
regime_hint: monetary tightening with strong labor market
failure_condition: If positive returns occur in 30% of cases, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Growth in housing starts (HOUST) during early-cycle recovery signals demand recovery, leading to positive S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: If returns are negative in 35% of cases with HOUST growth, the hypothesis fails.
